note: Colony rules (M5). Populations are people. Texts live in src/i18n/locales (colony.*).

modes.note: How colonists travel. unlock: capability needed (colony.mode.<id>). society: trait of the founded colony. Embryo ships carry a frozen stock that machines decant each year (decant per year).

sites.note: capacity in people (habitable scaled by world quality); food: produced / needed at the start technologies' level (closed sites add colony.closedFood); industry: output factor; crops: open-air agriculture (crop failures are worse, recycling is not needed).

growth.note: growth/year = rate x min(1, minFactor + surplus x (food - 1)) x (1 - pop/capacity); starving: -starvation x (1 - food).

output.note: materiel/year = industry x (pop/1000)^exponent x site x richness factor; research/year = research x log10(1 + pop/1000).

terraforming.note: years to turn a terraformable site habitable once full terraforming is known (processors halve it)

risks.note: Yearly chances and losses. Small colonies are hit harder and more often.

unrest.note: during unrest industry and research are multiplied by output

embryo.note: raised by machines; strange, unstable, drifting from the empire

ark.note: a closed people from centuries aboard

start.note: materiel at founding; a capital founded without history starts at capitalShare of its capacity

resilience.note: Large peoples weather disasters better: resilience = min(1, log10(1 + pop/1000) / scale); prion and crop chances x (1 - chance x resilience), losses and famine x (1 - loss x resilience).

preparation.note: Robotic preparatory missions (expansion.prepare). Seeders build habitats, nurseries and fields before colonists arrive. The work can fail, often silently.

lightEmbryo.note: embryo ships sent to a prepared site carry less: cheaper, but half the frozen stock dies if the site is not ready
